label: CRITICAL
intent_basis: State groups (Salt Typhoon, Iran-linked OT operators) and ransomware affiliates both prize edge access.
capability_basis: Edge CVEs reach KEV a median of one day after publication in 2026; Metasploit and Nuclei weaponize hundreds of new CVEs a year.
opportunity_basis: Ten edge vendors had flaws added to KEV in the last 30 days; every enterprise runs several of them.
drivers: CISA added PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) to KEV on 26 October with a 29 October deadline after a researcher logged 35 working shells on honeypots on 24 October; Siemens Ruggedcom APE1808 (PAN-OS) and Belden NetModule (no patch) confirm OT exposure; CYFIRMA sees a Lazarus-linked operator probing 216 vulnerable hosts including financial institutions; Microsoft shipped emergency .NET fixes for Brotli CVE-2026-111497; Rapid7 puts average time to exploitation at about three days.
so_what: Patch-or-isolate within 72 hours for KEV-listed edge devices; weekly triage of the early-warning list.

label: HIGH
intent_basis: DPRK revenue operations and organized crime target financial value directly.
capability_basis: DPRK theft above $2B in 2025; card-skimming fine-payment portals in the Gulf; cartel finance through front companies.
opportunity_basis: Payment flows are the target itself.
drivers: Intruders used MetaTrader logins taken from GMO Internet-hosted servers to place unauthorized trades at five Japanese FX brokers (confirmed 23-26 October), prompting an FSA directive and a refused US$50M ransom; CoinDCX lost about $16M from retired deposit wallets; DOJ arraigned an alleged launderer of $36.9M in Cambodia-based crypto scam proceeds.
so_what: Feed sanctions and fraud teams the same disruption-lane updates as security.

label: HIGH
intent_basis: Extortion crews and state actors both buy or steal valid sessions rather than exploit code.
capability_basis: ShinyHunters registers its own MFA devices after vishing the service desk; Salt Typhoon sits inside carriers that carry SMS codes.
opportunity_basis: Help desks reset MFA on a phone call; SaaS tokens outlive the users who granted them.
drivers: FBI: 140+ organisations and at least $70M tied to ShinyHunters; FBI says Salt Typhoon remains active.
so_what: Call-back verification for MFA resets; phishing-resistant factors; SaaS token reviews.

label: HIGH
intent_basis: Every tracked state and criminal actor uses it as an entry point.
capability_basis: Voice phishing of service desks, fake bank and fine-payment portals, and state phishing platforms such as FishHub.
opportunity_basis: Large workforces and outsourced help desks.
drivers: Iran-linked lures impersonate banks and payment portals; US seized Flax Typhoon's phishing infrastructure.
so_what: Train service-desk staff on vishing scripts; monitor lookalike payment domains.

label: HIGH
intent_basis: Financially motivated affiliates; leak-site claims against financial services more than doubled period on period.
capability_basis: Qilin and The Gentlemen run mature RaaS programs; MITRE added The Gentlemen in v20.
opportunity_basis: Exposure depends on third parties and edge-device hygiene.
drivers: Nord Security counts 2,894 Q3 attacks (up nearly 50% year on year), led by The Gentlemen (383) and Qilin (363); Arctic Wolf tracks hundreds of Teams 'IT support' vishing cases ending in Chaos ransomware; ASD cut off an Amadey loader controller from about 180,000 machines; GMO refused a US$50M demand.
so_what: Third-party extortion monitoring and incident-response retainer readiness.

label: HIGH
intent_basis: Extortion crews and state actors reach targets through vendors and software.
capability_basis: ATT&CK documents supply-chain techniques across many groups.
opportunity_basis: Large vendor estates and SaaS integrations.
drivers: GMO Internet's Desktop Cloud compromise (up to 26,739 servers) reached five regulated FX brokers through stored trading logins, with a US$50M extortion demand; DreamHost forced global password resets in an undisclosed incident from 23 October; ConnectWise (Storm-0940) and LiteLLM remain the reference cases.
so_what: Third-party breach monitoring and contract notification clauses.

label: ELEVATED
intent_basis: Iran-linked and pro-Russian hacktivists time DDoS to political and military events.
capability_basis: NoName057(16) pays volunteers; about 60 Iran-aligned groups run DDoS and defacement.
opportunity_basis: Public payment and authentication front ends are visible targets; mitigation contracts limit impact.
drivers: Iran war tempo before the US midterms; Russian hybrid campaign in Europe.
so_what: Confirm scrubbing capacity and runbooks for customer-facing services.

label: ELEVATED
intent_basis: DPRK places IT workers as insiders; recruited proxies support sabotage in Europe.
capability_basis: Third-country fronts pass interviews and background checks.
opportunity_basis: Remote technical hiring through staffing vendors.
drivers: DOJ says DPRK IT workers reached at least 70 US companies and now recruit US facilitators; proxies recruited online for European sabotage.
so_what: Identity proofing at hire and device-location monitoring.
